entry.title: fix(sync): scope vercel reasoning menus to what the gateway bridge ho…
entry.content:
fix(sync): scope vercel reasoning menus to what the gateway bridge honors

Empirical probes against the xAI API plus the gateway reasoning bridge
(materializeXai clamps none/minimal->low and xhigh/max->high, and only
grok-3-mini/4.3/4.5/4.6 families support effort at all) show the
previously restored menus over-advertised:

- grok-4.3: drop none (gateway clamps it to low; none is a real off
  switch only on xAI direct, verified 0 reasoning tokens)
- grok-4.6: drop xhigh (gateway clamps it to high)
- grok-4.20-multi-agent(+beta): revert to empty, the bridge ignores
  effort entirely for this family, so a menu would be decorative

gpt-5-codex keeps low/medium/high (the gateway OpenAI dialect passes
effort through; direct verification blocked, the model 404s on our
OpenAI key).

entry.title: fix(sync): map spacexai to canonical xai metadata and treat empty rea…
entry.content:
fix(sync): map spacexai to canonical xai metadata and treat empty reasoning_options as unset

The gateway renamed its xai provider to spacexai, but
CANONICAL_PROVIDER_PREFIXES had no spacexai entry, so the Vercel sync
created the renamed files without base_model resolution. With no base
to inherit from, preserveReasoningOptions stamped reasoning_options = []
on every new spacexai file, and the existing ?? base preservation kept
that empty array forever, erasing the effort menus the old xai files
carried.

- Add spacexai to CANONICAL_PROVIDER_PREFIXES so the renamed models
  factor onto the canonical xai metadata again (verified via
  models:sync vercel: base_model restored, duplicated fields factored
  out, no other output changes).
- In buildVercelModel, treat an empty existing reasoning_options array
  as unset so it no longer shadows the route base's menu.
- Re-author the lost effort menus, mirroring the first-party xAI
  entries: grok-4.3 (none/low/medium/high), grok-4.5 (low/medium/high),
  grok-4.6 and grok-4.20-multi-agent(+beta) (low/medium/high/xhigh),
  and gpt-5-codex (low/medium/high, matching what the gateway
  advertises today). Models whose first-party entry also declares no
  controls (grok-4.20-reasoning, grok-build-0.1, grok-4.1-fast-*) keep
  the empty array.
